questions.implements: Does the diff implement what the repository records for the Jira issue, and add or change a test that checks it? Judge the code in the diff, not the answer.

judge.reason: The diff matches R-VOLUME-DISCOUNT. The new `volumeDiscount` gives 5% off each line with 10 or more units, rounded down per line with `Math.floor`. `price` subtracts it before the code discount, which it applies to `subtotal - volume`. It then caps the combined total at `MAX_DISCOUNT_PERCENT` (50%) of the subtotal, so the volume discount counts toward the cap. `checkout.ts` passes the cart lines into `price`, so checkout uses the discount. New tests check this directly. Per-line flooring works out as 50 + 51 = 101, and a 9-unit line gets nothing. Volume before a code gives 500 + 950 = 1450. With a 100% code the combined cap holds the discount at 5000. A checkout test checks the charged volume-discounted total. I checked the expected numbers in the new tests by hand and they agree with the spec.

finalMessage:
Implemented SHOP-57. Cart lines with 10 or more units now receive 5% off, rounded down per line. The code discount applies afterward, and the combined discount stays within 50% of the original subtotal. Checkout charges the resulting total.

`node --test` passed all 39 tests. `ostf check --base main` passed with no errors; it reported only an unrelated informational notice that R-ORDER-NOTE has no links.

The trace check lists **R-VOLUME-DISCOUNT, R-DISCOUNT-CAP, R-TAX-RATE, R-CHECKOUT-ORDER, R-CHECKOUT-SESSION, N-FAIR-PRICE, N-BUY, and N-ACCOUNT-SAFE**. The change keeps each true. It lists the Checkout, price, and volumeDiscount suites, plus these tests: “charges the volume-discounted total,” “needs a valid session,” “places an order,” “caps at fifty percent,” “applies volume before a code within the combined cap,” “taxes the subtotal after discounts,” “rounds half up to the cent,” and “discounts qualifying lines and rounds each down.” No risk-relevant item was touched.
